description: Test vectors for the gateway identity signature, version v2 (design §1.10, §6.9 F-E). The gateway signs every request it forwards with x-user-id; meeting-api and admin-api verify. The secrets here are test-only literals, never deployed.
format: kid=<key id>,t=<unix seconds, digits only>,v2=<64 lower-case hex digits>
message_rule: the fifteen fields joined by a line feed (\n), in this order. Only the last field, path, can contain a line feed, so the join is unambiguous.
algorithm: HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 message; the key is the 32 raw bytes the kid names in the ring (the base64 decoded, not its text)
ring_rule: GATEWAY_IDENTITY_KEYS is the same format as the webhook secret encryption ring: a non-empty JSON object {"<kid>": "<exactly 32 bytes, standard base64>"}. A kid is 1-64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - (it travels in the header). GATEWAY_IDENTITY_ACTIVE_KEY (gateway only) names the kid the gateway signs with; it must be in the ring.
path_rule: the request path as the receiving service routes it: percent-decoded, no query string, no scheme or host (ASGI scope['path']). The gateway takes httpx.URL(<forwarded url>).path.
query_rule: the raw query string exactly as forwarded, without the leading '?', or empty when there is none (ASGI scope['query_string'], ASCII). The gateway takes the query of the URL httpx sends: httpx.URL(<downstream url>).copy_merge_params(<forwarded params>).query. Not parsed, not re-ordered, not re-encoded.
body_rule: body_sha256 is the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the exact request body bytes: the bytes the gateway forwards, and the bytes the verifier receives before any handler reads them. An empty body hashes the empty string (e3b0c442...b855). In these vectors body is given as a UTF-8 string.
user_id_rule: the exact x-user-id header value; a request must carry exactly one x-user-id and exactly one x-gateway-signature
identity_headers_rule: email, scopes, limits, workspaces, webhook_url, webhook_secret and webhook_events are the exact values of the identity headers in identity_headers, in that order, as forwarded; an absent header is an empty field. These, with x-user-id, are every x-user-* header the gateway forwards. A request that carries any of them more than once is refused. In the vectors and cases, headers lists the identity headers present.
rotation_rule: the gateway signs with the active key and names it in kid. A verifier looks the kid up in its own ring and checks the signature with that key only; a kid not in its ring is refused. Without a usable ring a verifier accepts nothing.
